title: Explicit mapping retry with preserved source and attempt history
changes: Accept one unambiguous JSON object with an optional single Markdown code fence, without repairing model content.
Offer one explicit smaller-request retry after a proven incomplete first mapping, preserving the original attempt.
Bind all original source objects and selected whole code units to versioned request partitions.
Require current source, target and three fresh consents before creating a deterministic retry child.
Retain a validated parent and child in source history without duplicate or automatic dispatch.
Distinguish a proven terminal pre-execution mapping failure from unknown work in verifier admission.
limitations: Server-side preparation must be configured and tested by the operator; a source release does not enable it.
This hosted preparation route accepts one FMB per request; MMB, OLB and PLL require the separate supported preparation route.
The focused prototype profile, current authority endpoint and private browser worker require explicit operator configuration and live checks.
Real-file OPAF-to-APEX import, authenticated runtime and downloadable export acceptance remain pending.
Corrected prompts remain operator-selected resources. One saved real-source partition passed an approved reviewer-only retest; the complete application remains unverified.
Retry is limited to a proven first-mapper coverage failure. Unknown operations, later-stage failures and chained retries require operator reconciliation.
Technical identifiers are retained; redaction receipts are not complete PII certification or processing permission.
APEX generated, technical checks passed and business acceptance remain separate.
A prototype export does not prove clean-schema reimport, customer-target compatibility or business equivalence.
Release notes describe software changes, not proof of a successful conversion.
